title: A Correlation Analysis of Penguin Flipper Length and Body Mass
text:
Introduction

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

df = sns.load_dataset('penguins')
sns.set_context('talk')

RQ: Is there a correlation between penguins’ flipper length and body mass?
Penguins have different body sizes and flipper lengths, and this project uses Python and Quarto to examine whether these two characteristics are correlated.


Literature Review
Previous research by Gorman et al. (2014) examined physical differences among Antarctic penguins and found that body size varies across species and sexes [@gorman2014ecological].
These findings suggest that penguins’ physical characteristics may be related to each other.


Method
Given that we have two columns of continuous data, flipper length measured in millimeters and body mass measured in grams, we will examine their relationship using simple Pearson correlation analysis.
We will also use a scatterplot to visualize the relationship between these two variables.


Results

corr_val = np.array(
    df[['flipper_length_mm', 'body_mass_g']].corr()
)[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > .8:
    narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > .4:
    narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
    narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -.4:
    narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"

Using the simple Pearson correlation approach, these data produce a correlation coefficient of 0.87120.
Given this result, we conclude that there is a very strong positive correlation between penguins’ flipper length and body mass.

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))

sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    y='body_mass_g',
    x='flipper_length_mm',
    ax=ax
)

plt.ylabel('Body Mass (g)')
plt.xlabel('Flipper Length (mm)')
plt.show()







Figure 1: A scatterplot of penguin flipper length and body mass







Discussion
The results show that penguins with longer flippers generally have greater body mass, suggesting a strong positive correlation between these two characteristics.
However, correlation does not imply causation, and differences in species or sex may also influence this relationship.

sns.lmplot(
    data=df,
    y="body_mass_g",
    x="flipper_length_mm"
)









sns.jointplot(
    data=df,
